name: Ambient 44-bar arrangement map: low pad + light percussion, high pad at bar 5, piano at bar 13, shaker at ~bar 17, a mid-track strip-back to shaker/hat that sets up a return with new piano chords, and a coda that ends on the piano
goal: Turn a 4-5 bar ambient loop into a ~44-bar song with a deliberate shape: set the tone with a low pad and sparse rim/cymbal (bars 1-5), add a high pad at bar 5 for gentle rising action, add piano around bar 13 and shaker around bar 16-17 to reach the 'full track', then strip the main percussion and low pad (keep only shaker and hat) for about 8 bars so the ending feels near, bring everything back around bar 33 with piano chords the listener has not heard yet (the spike of interest), stop the percussion half a bar early and end on the calming piano chords at bar 45 as a coda. Voice the new chords so the low pad only plays the notes that change while the piano replays the full chord every bar.

source.title: HOW TO PRODUCE AMBIENT MUSIC - ARRANGING YOUR AMBIENT SONG
source.transcript_note: Auto-generated YouTube transcript; garbled in places (percussion names approximated)

prerequisites: A DAW with a short ambient loop (low pad, high pad, rim/cymbal, piano, shaker) already written
Group/submix tracks and colour-coded tracks set up (the source does this before arranging)

inputs.name: loop_layers
inputs.description: Pad low, pad high, rim shot, cymbal, piano, shaker (or equivalents).

outputs.name: arrangement_map
outputs.description: Bar-by-bar entry/exit list for each layer, plus the coda.

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Approximate bar numbers come from a spoken walkthrough; treat them as a template, not exact positions.
YouTube Show transcript is auto-generated and partly garbled; steps are approximated from the spoken description only.
Arrangement only: EQ/mixing are out of scope (separate episode).

steps.action: Colour-code tracks and put related layers on group/submix tracks so entries and exits are easy to see.
steps.expect: Arrangement view is readable per layer.

steps.action: Bars 1-5: play only the low pad plus a sparse rim shot and cymbal to set the tone (calm, slightly upbeat, comfortable).
steps.expect: Mood is established with minimal parts.

steps.action: Bar 5: add the high-pitched pad for a little movement; keep it non-intense. Hold this for ~8 more bars.
Bar 13: add piano; around bar 16-17 add the shaker so you reach what sounds like the full track.
Strip back: remove the rim shot, cymbal and low pad so only the shaker and a hi-hat-like element remain; hold ~8 bars. The listener may think the song is ending.
steps.expect: Density drops sharply; only light percussion left.

steps.action: Bar ~33: bring everything back (low pad, rim, cymbal) and add piano chords and melody the listener has not heard before to spike interest. Hold ~9 bars.
steps.expect: Return feels fresh, not a repeat.

steps.action: Voice the new chords: low pad plays only the notes that change between chords (holding up to two bars) while the piano replays the whole chord every bar with full-bar note lengths; automate volume where needed.
steps.expect: Pad stays smooth, piano re-articulates each bar.

steps.action: End: stop the percussion about half a bar before the end so it finishes at an odd angle, leaving the calm piano chords to finish at bar 45 as a coda.
steps.expect: Last thing heard is the familiar calming piano.

verification: Print an entry/exit table: each layer's first and last bar matches the map within a few bars.
At the strip-back only shaker and hat play; at the return at least one chord set is new vs bars 1-32.
